questions.q: Why can't a single relationship field represent a many-to-many relationship, like Contacts to Campaigns?
options: A relationship field holds one value pointing at one record; it can't hold a list of relationships that each carry their own extra data
Salesforce fields are limited to exactly two related records maximum
Many-to-many relationships are actually impossible to represent in any database
Contacts and Campaigns are not allowed to relate to each other at all in Salesforce
questions.explain: A field stores one value; many-to-many needs a structure that can represent many individual pairings, each potentially with its own data.

questions.q: What is a junction object, structurally, per this lesson?
options: A custom object with exactly two Master-Detail relationships, one to each of the two objects it connects
A special Salesforce field type that stores multiple record IDs at once
A report that displays two objects side by side
A Lookup relationship that happens to be created twice
questions.explain: The junction object pattern is built from two Master-Detail relationships on one custom object.

questions.q: What is Salesforce's real, standard junction object for connecting Contacts (or Leads) to Campaigns?
options: CampaignMember
ContactCampaignLink
CampaignContact
MemberJunction
questions.explain: CampaignMember is Salesforce's actual standard junction object for the Contact/Lead-to-Campaign many-to-many relationship.

questions.q: Why does CampaignMember's Status field have to live on the junction record rather than directly on Contact or Campaign, per this lesson?
options: Because the junction record is the only place in the data model that represents one specific Contact-Campaign pairing, which is what the status describes
Because Contact and Campaign objects don't support picklist fields
Because Status is actually a standard field on Contact, not on CampaignMember
There's no real reason -- it's an arbitrary Salesforce design choice
questions.explain: A Contact is in many campaigns with potentially different statuses each; only the junction record represents one specific pairing.

questions.q: Why is it correct that a junction object uses Master-Detail relationships (not Lookup) to each side, based on what you learned last lesson?
options: Master-Detail's mandatory link ensures the junction record can't exist without both parents it's connecting
Lookup relationships are not technically allowed to exist on custom objects
Master-Detail relationships are simply easier to create than Lookup relationships
It's not actually correct -- junction objects always use Lookup relationships in real orgs
questions.explain: A junction record only makes sense if it's tied to both sides -- Master-Detail's mandatory, required link enforces exactly that.
